title: MA2H GET Message Body (v0.5)
description: Body of GET /v1/messages/{id}: the original message plus current `status`, the Hub-assigned `id`, and (once terminal) the embedded `response`.

allOf.$comment: An ask/task's top-level status is ALWAYS the §7 resolution track (spec §8.2/§14.2) — mailbox states (queued/bounced/acknowledged/delivered) live under `delivery`; a bounce surfaces here only as its cancelled/dismissed auto-resolution.
A human-inbox notify is delivered-on-acceptance (spec §5.1) and has no other state.
An addressed notify's lifecycle IS the §14.2 delivery track (spec §5.1).
Without `to` this GET is the agent->human leg: the delivery object is the RESPONSE track (spec §14.2) — mailbox-only states cannot appear.
With `to` this GET is the sender's authoritative mailbox view (spec §8.2/§14.2) — the response-track delivered-to-agent cannot appear.

status.description: Lifecycle status (spec §7). v0.5 adds `queued`/`bounced`/`acknowledged` for ADDRESSED messages: an addressed notify's lifecycle IS the delivery track (queued -> delivered -> acknowledged, or terminal bounced/expired, spec §14.2); an addressed ask/task keeps the §7 resolution machinery here (open -> terminals — an undeliverable track terminal auto-resolves it cancelled/dismissed) with the mailbox track surfaced under `delivery`.

response.description: Present once the message is terminal (ask/task). Embeds the full Response envelope.

delivery.description: Additive receipt track (spec §14.2), orthogonal to `status`/`response`. Present on a Hub offering the ack primitive. For a human-inbox ask/task this is the response track the human reads (delivered-to-agent -> acknowledged, plus the v0.5 terminal `expired` = the answer was NEVER seen, spec §14.2). For an ADDRESSED message this same object on the sender's authoritative §8.2 pull carries the mailbox track (queued -> delivered -> acknowledged, or terminal bounced/expired, spec §14.2): on `bounced`, a present `delivered_at` means seen-then-orphaned and an absent one means never seen (the receipt `prior` distinction, spec §8.7). A delivery-track `expired` always means never delivered.

delivered_at.description: When the receiving party got the message (mailbox entry drained, or Response push-2xx / agent GET).

ack.description: The ack envelope, present once state is `acknowledged`.

allOf.$comment: Delivery honesty (spec §14.2): queued = not delivered yet, and a delivery-track `expired` MUST mean NEVER delivered — a body claiming both delivered_at and one of these states would be the exact false belief the track exists to kill. bounced deliberately allows delivered_at: its presence is the seen-then-orphaned signal (receipt prior: delivered), its absence never-seen.
